bach_invention_01.song: Bach Two-Part Invention No.1 in C major (BWV 772)
bach_invention_01.key_finding: pianoplayer wins on Bach RH scalar passages (Soft 0.734 vs ArLSTM 0.406) — direction REVERSES from Canon. Two contributing explanations: (1) Bach RH is exactly the scalar/thumb-under scenario Parncutt cost model was designed for, (2) rule-based GT's single-note-rule structurally aligns with pianoplayer cost model behavior on stepwise. Bach LH remains ArLSTM-dominant (0.878 vs 0.391), consistent with pp's universal LH ring atrophy bias. Logical implication: Logic Track is best-when-style-dependent; current default (ArLSTM) is correct for Canon-style and Summer-style but not Bach Invention-style.

beethoven_op2no1_mvt1.song: Beethoven Piano Sonata No.1 in F minor Op.2 No.1, mvt 1 (Allegro)
beethoven_op2no1_mvt1.key_finding: Beethoven RH: pianoplayer wins (Soft 0.662 vs ArLSTM 0.359) — consistent with Bach RH pattern (pp wins scalar passages). Beethoven LH SURPRISES: ArLSTM only barely wins Soft (0.379 vs 0.335), and ArLSTM actually LOSES Hard (0.190 vs 0.317). Both models score poorly (< 0.4 Soft), unlike Canon/Bach LH where ArLSTM dominated. Likely contributing factors: (1) Beethoven LH is angular (chord stabs + scalar runs alternating), not the regular Alberti or contrapuntal texture ArLSTM saw in PIG training; (2) HAND_SPLIT=60 misassigns some notes during cross-hand passages typical of Classical sonatas; (3) high artifact-skip count (446 RH + 162 LH) suggests MIDI quality issues. Revised thesis claim: ArLSTM LH dominance is texture-dependent, not universal.
